display_name: Art. 336 to 336b OR (abusive termination of an employment contract): whole, layer 1 plus employee and employer seats, from the German text
maintainer: Legalese (written by a single Sonnet 5.5 agent working alone from the brief; no human maintainer assigned yet)
method: a single Sonnet 5.5 agent working alone from the brief, with the encoding-a-subject and writing-l4-rules skills and the Commons guide copies; no other encoding or formalisation was read
seat: employee: one person in one employment, asking on facts they can state whether a notice of termination (their employer's or their own) is abusive, what they can claim and how much at most, and by when they must object and sue; second seat: the employer, asking whether a notice it gave or received is abusive, what it can be made to pay and how much at most, and what the other side must do and by when to keep a claim; the employer seat also asks, as the party that received a notice from its employee, its own objection, claim, last days and forfeiture

scope.encoded: Art. 336, Art. 336a and Art. 336b of the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR, SR 220), whole: the grounds of abusive termination (336(1) for either party, 336(2) for the employer, 336(3) protection of an employee representative after a transfer), the compensation and its ceilings (336a), and the objection and the 180-day action (336b)
scope.not_encoded: the amount of the compensation (the judge's; the encoding answers NOTHING and computes the ceiling only); Art. 333 and 335f (context, no rows); Art. 335 to 335d (notice periods, mass dismissal: asked as plain facts); Art. 336c and 336d; the procedure after an action is pending; case law
scope.edition: Fedlex consolidated version in German applicable from 2026-10-01 (the deposit records that the three Articles read the same in the version applicable from 2027-07-01; the encoder did not check this)

not_reviewed: No domain expert has read this encoding against the text. The source file is a script rendering of Fedlex's consolidated version, not the official text; nothing here is verified against the official text. The English in identifiers, descriptions and notes is the encoder's gloss, not the law. The marginal readings (a) and (b) of the rule of 2026-10-29 and the 31 fork entries in NOTES.md are for a lawyer to settle.
